In [[mathematics]], a '''Hadamard manifold''', named after [[Jacques Hadamard]] — more often called a '''Cartan–Hadamard manifold''', after [[Élie Cartan]] — is a [[Riemannian manifold]] <math>(M, g)</math> that is [[Complete metric space|complete]] and [[Simply connected space|simply connected]] and has everywhere non-positive [[sectional curvature]].<ref name=Li2102>{{cite book|last=Li|first=Peter|title=Geometric Analysis|year=2012|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9781107020641|pages=381|doi=10.1017/CBO9781139105798}}</ref><ref name=Lang1893>{{cite book|last=Lang|first=Serge|title=Fundamentals of Differential Geometry, Volume 160|year=1989|publisher=Springer|isbn=9780387985930|pages=252–253}}</ref> By [[Cartan–Hadamard theorem]] all Cartan–Hadamard manifolds are diffeomorphic to the Euclidean space <math>\mathbb{R}^n.</math> Furthermore it follows from the [[Hopf–Rinow theorem]] that every pairs of points in a Cartan–Hadamard manifold may be connected by a unique geodesic segment. Thus Cartan–Hadamard manifolds are some of the closest relatives of <math>\mathbb{R}^n.</math>

==Examples==

The [[Euclidean space]] <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> with its usual metric is a Cartan–Hadamard manifold with constant sectional curvature equal to <math>0.</math>

Standard <math>n</math>-dimensional [[hyperbolic space]] <math>\mathbb{H}^n</math> is a Cartan–Hadamard manifold with constant sectional curvature equal to <math>-1.</math>

==Properties== 

In Cartan-Hadamard manifolds, the map <math>\exp_p : \operatorname{T}M_p \to M</math> is a [[diffeomorphism]] for all <math>p \in M.</math>
